clips.send: Start with any right triangle. Call the two short sides (the legs) a and b , and the long side opposite the right angle, the hypotenuse, c .
clips.text: Start with any right triangle. Call the two short sides (the legs) a and b, and the long side opposite the right angle, the hypotenuse, c.

clips.send: Now slide the same four triangles into new positions inside the same big square. Watch the empty space change shape.
clips.text: Now slide the same four triangles into new positions inside the same big square. Watch the empty space change shape...

clips.send: Now build a square on each side. The square on side a has area a squared , on side b area b squared , and on the hypotenuse area c squared .
clips.text: Now build a square on each side. The square on side a has area a 2, on side b area b 2, and on the hypotenuse area c 2.

clips.send: Try a 3-4-5 triangle and count unit squares: 3 squared equals 9 and 4 squared equals 16 . The big square holds 5 squared equals 25 , and 9 plus 16 equals 25 . Coincidence? Let’s find out why it always works.
clips.text: Try a 3-4-5 triangle and count unit squares: 3 2 = 9 and 4 2 = 16. The big square holds 5 2 = 25, and 9 + 16 = 25. Coincidence? Let’s find out why it always works.

clips.send: The empty space is now two squares: a squared and b squared . Same big square, same four triangles, so the leftover area must be the same both times!
clips.text: The empty space is now two squares: a 2 and b 2. Same big square, same four triangles, so the leftover area must be the same both times!

clips.send: So the area of the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the areas of the squares on the legs: a squared plus b squared equals c squared
clips.text: So the area of the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the areas of the squares on the legs: a 2 + b 2 = c 2

clips.send: Use it! A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. Then c squared equals 36 plus 64 equals 100 , so c equals the square root of 100 equals 10 . The theorem turns two lengths into the third.
clips.text: Use it! A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. Then c 2 = 36 + 64 = 100, so c = sqrt 100 = 10. The theorem turns two lengths into the third.

clips.send: Here is the trick. Make a big square with side a plus b , and place four copies of our triangle in its corners. The hole left in the middle is a tilted square with side c , so its area is c squared .
clips.text: Here is the trick. Make a big square with side a + b, and place four copies of our triangle in its corners. The hole left in the middle is a tilted square with side c, so its area is c 2.

clips.send: 试试 3-4-5 三角形，数一数小方格： 3的平方 等于 9 , 4的平方 等于 16 。大正方形里有 5的平方 等于 25 个，而 9 加 16 等于 25 。是巧合吗？我们来看看为什么它总是成立。
clips.text: 试试 3-4-5 三角形，数一数小方格：3 2 = 9,4 2 = 16。大正方形里有 5 2 = 25 个，而 9 + 16 = 25。是巧合吗？我们来看看为什么它总是成立。

clips.send: 现在把同样的四个三角形在同一个大正方形里挪到新的位置。注意观察空白部分形状的变化……
clips.text: 现在把同样的四个三角形在同一个大正方形里挪到新的位置。注意观察空白部分形状的变化……

clips.send: 用起来！一个直角三角形的直角边是 6 和 8。那么 c的平方 等于 36 加 64 等于 100 ，所以 c 等于 根号100 等于 10 。知道两条边，就能求出第三条。
clips.text: 用起来！一个直角三角形的直角边是 6 和 8。那么 c 2 = 36 + 64 = 100，所以 c = sqrt 100 = 10。知道两条边，就能求出第三条。

clips.send: 现在在每条边上各画一个正方形。边 a 上的正方形面积是 a的平方 ，边 b 上的是 b的平方 ，斜边上的是 c的平方 。
clips.text: 现在在每条边上各画一个正方形。边 a 上的正方形面积是 a 2，边 b 上的是 b 2，斜边上的是 c 2。

clips.send: 空白部分现在变成了两个正方形： a的平方 和 b的平方 。大正方形一样，四个三角形也一样，所以两次剩下的面积一定相等!
clips.text: 空白部分现在变成了两个正方形：a 2 和 b 2。大正方形一样，四个三角形也一样，所以两次剩下的面积一定相等!

clips.send: 从任意一个直角三角形开始。把两条较短的边（直角边）叫作 a 和 b ，把直角对面最长的边——斜边——叫作 c 。
clips.text: 从任意一个直角三角形开始。把两条较短的边（直角边）叫作 a 和 b，把直角对面最长的边——斜边——叫作 c。

clips.send: 所以斜边上正方形的面积，等于两条直角边上正方形面积之和： a的平方 加 b的平方 等于 c的平方
clips.text: 所以斜边上正方形的面积，等于两条直角边上正方形面积之和：a 2 + b 2 = c 2

clips.send: 关键的一招来了。做一个边长为 a 加 b 的大正方形，把我们的三角形复制四份放在四个角上。中间留下的空洞是一个倾斜的正方形，边长是 c ，所以面积是 c的平方 。
clips.text: 关键的一招来了。做一个边长为 a + b 的大正方形，把我们的三角形复制四份放在四个角上。中间留下的空洞是一个倾斜的正方形，边长是 c，所以面积是 c 2。
